prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UK Independence Party Manifesto 2005 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core aim
- Leave the European Union to restore UK sovereignty, lawmaking and democratic accountability. Repeal the European Communities Act, stop EU budget payments, and run a two-year transition to replace EU-derived laws and policies (farming, fishing, etc.) with UK ones. Maintain trade with the EU via bilateral deals and expand global trade (Commonwealth, NAFTA, WTO seat regained).

Economy and tax
- Deregulation: Scrap or amend EU-origin regulations, prioritising relief for small businesses; remove burdens like the Working Time Directive; presume repeal unless a strong case exists.
- Budget: Redirect the claimed £1bn/year net EU contribution to increase state pensions by £2/week. Temporarily borrow £3bn/year to fund immediate tax cuts and defence; repay as growth rises from deregulation and tax reform.
- Immediate tax measures: Halve council tax for all households; scrap the 10% income tax band; restore dividend tax credits to pension funds; raise the inheritance tax threshold to £500,000.
- Long-term tax reform: Merge National Insurance with income tax; replace VAT with a wholesale sales tax; consider a low flat tax to simplify and spur growth.

Health and welfare
- NHS: End central micromanagement and targets; restore local control; bring back matrons; scrap Strategic Health Authorities; extend GP hours; prioritise clinical judgment; consider complementary private insurance; remove EU limits on supplements and doctors’ hours.
- Welfare: Simplify, reduce means-testing, cut admin costs, and avoid ineffective work programmes.
- Pensions: Immediate uplift and restore pension fund tax credits; unfreeze expatriate pensions; accept need to save more/work longer; reject mass immigration as a pension fix.

Education
- Schools: More autonomy; scrap SATs and QCA; empower heads to exclude; require sports, history and trips; enable specialisation and limited selection; expand assisted places, vouchers/tax rebates for private options.
- Universities: Close low-quality courses; fully fund high-standard ones; cancel top-up fees; restore maintenance grants; scrap student loans; charge EU students full fees; expand technical colleges.

Law, immigration, and society
- Law and order: Local accountability of police; cut paperwork; tougher, credible sentencing; strengthen magistrates; build prisons; defend jury trial; reject EU Corpus Juris.
- Immigration: Target near-zero net immigration via a points system, equal rules for EU/non-EU, stricter family routes, embarkation controls, Britishness tests, health checks, safe-third-country rule, faster deportations; amend Human Rights Act/interpretations as needed; no quotas.
- Rights and freedoms: Repeal the Human Rights Act; drop ID cards; repeal the Hunting Act; resist overregulation and “rights culture.”

Agriculture, fisheries, energy, environment, transport
- Farming: Leave CAP; replace with guaranteed minimum prices/deficiency payments; cut bureaucracy; support local abattoirs, markets, green/organic methods, hill farms; consider Milk Marketing Board; biosecurity.
- Fisheries: Exit CFP; restore control and enforcement; licensing for sustainable practices; fallow zones.
- Defence/foreign: Increase spending; reverse regiment cuts; buy British; deploy only in national interest; stay in NATO; exit EU defence schemes.
- Energy: Stop wind turbines; build new nuclear (fission); support clean coal; fund fusion research.
- Environment: UK-led rules; curb waste; boost recycling; protect green belt; ban GM crop planting until proven safe.
- Transport: Invest in roads and rail upgrades; review rail structure (possible reintegration); resist EU transport directives; consider higher motorway limits; focus speed cameras on proven danger sites.

Governance
- Uphold monarchy, Commons, Lords (oppose elected Lords); binding referendums when 5% of voters petition within six months. More local authority autonomy and funding (return business rates and stamp duty); scrap English regional assemblies/quangos; consider “English days” at Westminster. Reject the EU Constitution.
